messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT - High error + request rate on /v1/embeddings detected (region: us-east-1). Auto-page to oncall.
Emma Chen: I’m on it, picking up the page. quick look: error rate up ~7% and tail latency spiking.
Emma Chen: Logs show large number of very small, repetitive embedding requests from a handful of IPs and user agents. smells like scrape farm.
Sanjay Patel: seeing same. lots of identical prompts and short payloads, high fanout to batch workers.
Lorna McBride: can we slice quota or enable stricter per-key rate-limits while we triage?
Emma Chen: yes. plan: 1) apply dynamic throttle for suspicious client fingerprints 2) push a WAF captcha challenge on high-rate sources 3) temporarily disable embeddings_batch on public endpoints to reduce concurrency.
Sanjay Patel: I’ll prepare a rate-slice rule. suggest: 100 rps -> 20 rps for offending keys, with exponential backoff header.
Emma Chen: good. Sanjay, can you roll that? Lorna, can you stage a WAF rule to challenge (captcha) for the IP ranges? Diego, FYI - you’ll get handoff in 20m.
Sanjay Patel: applying rate-slice now:
```
POST /internal/rate_rules
{
  "matcher": "client_fingerprint in ('fp:abc123','fp:def456')",
  "action": "throttle",
  "limit_rps": 20,
  "scope": "api_key"
}
```
Sanjay Patel: rule applied, returning 202. watching metrics.
Lorna McBride: WAF rule staged to challenge on those IPs and UA patterns, rolling to edge in 30s.
deploy-bot: deploy started: waf/challenge-rule v2026 -> edge-policies (canary 10%).
Sanjay Patel: within 60s we see reduced fanout to batch workers, success rate recovering from 93% to 98%. latency tail dropping.
Emma Chen: good. still seeing some clients fall back to different IPs. need broader fallback: enable per-account quota caps and disable batch endpoint that amplifies cost.
Lorna McBride: disabling batch embeddings on public:
```
rbctl set-feature embeddings_batch_enabled false --env=prod
```
Lorna McBride: disabled. pushing notice to status page and support.
support-bot: Posted incident advisory: "We are mitigating a large-scale scraper affecting embeddings. Some embedding batch requests are temporarily unavailable. We will provide updates."
Emma Chen: CS notified. Any customers seeing errors?
Diego Alvarez: forwarded a support ticket from a customer in APAC experiencing 429s. they are not in the high-rate list; likely collateral. we should add a grace rule for verified customers.
Sanjay Patel: adding allowlist for enterprise keys to bypass throttle:
```
POST /internal/rate_rules
{
  "matcher": "api_key in ('ent-01','ent-02')",
  "action": "allow",
  "scope": "api_key"
}
```
Sanjay Patel: allowlist live. Diego, can you validate customer traffic?
Diego Alvarez: validated, their requests are now passing. they confirmed degraded but functional. asked for ETA on full recovery.
Emma Chen: ETA: 30m for stable, full rollback in 2 hours if no new patterns. open items: 1) watch for new IP churn 2) evaluate longer-term WAF fingerprinting rules 3) postmortem owner assignment.
Lorna McBride: recommend we capture a sample of offending requests and add hash-based fingerprinting rather than IPs, to avoid churn.
Sanjay Patel: agreed. saving sample set to /mnt/incidents/2205001234/samples.log:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z fp:abc123 ua:curl/7.85 ip:3.5.67.89 prompt_len:12
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z fp:def456 ua:python-requests/2.28 ip:3.5.67.90 prompt_len:8
```
Emma Chen: handing off to Diego for next shift. Diego: summary -> dynamic throttle applied to fingerprints, WAF captcha challenge deployed to edge, batch embeddings disabled, enterprise allowlist added, status page live. watch window: 2h.
Diego Alvarez: taking handoff. I’ll keep monitoring and escalate if any regression. please add any follow-ups here.
Emma Chen: thanks team. leaving notes: investigate whether we can push challenge earlier in the chain, and add automated rollback for batch-disable after pattern subsides.
incident-bot: Incident assigned -> oncall: Diego Alvarez. Priority: P1 (mitigated).
Diego Alvarez: will run a post-incident capture and schedule postmortem. tagging @SRE and @Sec for deeper fingerprinting analysis.
Emma Chen: closing my active oncall thread, leaving the incident in Diego's hands. :thumbsup:
